name: gridquest-frozen-oracle-reward-v1
declared: 2026-10-31, before implementation or hunting of goal_reward_missing
oracle: v2 check_transition, unchanged from the 23 October full-state contract
defect_description: On a successful key-and-goal entry under sparse reward, return 0.0 instead of the declared 1.0. Keep position, key, coin, score, termination and reported success unchanged.
design_boundary: The frozen v2 oracle compares position, key, coin and score, not the step reward. This challenge is deliberately chosen after reading that boundary; it is not an independent unseen-defect sample.
prediction: The unchanged v2 oracle reports no violation even when the reward fault is exposed. Report any contrary detection rather than changing the contract.
maps: default layout plus all eight frozen gridquest-unseen-v1 layouts
hunt_rule: Use the existing hunt policy and v2 oracle. Add only the new defect name to its allow-list; do not change action selection, stopping, reset or oracle logic. Run each defective and clean map/policy/seed once. A violation is detection; misses are right-censored at 1200 steps.
exposure_probe: For each of nine maps and five seeds, separately drive a scripted key-then-goal path on the defective environment and record whether a successful goal entry returned 0.0. This probe does not feed the hunt or oracle and is not counted as a detection.
metrics: defective detections and clean false alarms per policy on default (n=5) and held-out (n=40) maps, with Wilson 95% intervals
violation kinds, censored misses, and discovery-step mean/median only among detections
scripted exposure-probe successes out of 45 map/seed runs
reading_rules: A zero detection count with 45/45 scripted exposure proves this specific reward fault is outside the v2 public-state contract, not that every policy reached the fault.
Any clean false alarm is reported and invalidates a clean detection claim for that map set.
No tuning, p-value or generalization claim follows from this adversarial synthetic defect.
